title: Summation and Product Notation
learning_objectives: Read Σ and Π notation and translate it into a loop
Check a closed-form formula against a loop
Explain why math.fsum is more accurate than repeated +
entry_point: summation(f, start, stop); product(f, start, stop); mean(xs); sum_of_squares(n); accurate_sum(xs)
hints: `for i in range(start, stop + 1): total += f(i)` — note the `+ 1`.
A product starts from 1. For the mean, `summation(lambda i: xs[i], 0, len(xs) - 1) / len(xs)`.
`n * (n + 1) * (2 * n + 1) // 6` is exact because the product is always divisible by 6.

failure_feedback.advice: Include the last index: loop over `range(start, stop + 1)`.
Start the sum at 0 and the product at 1; an empty range leaves them unchanged.
Divide the sum by the number of items and raise ValueError for an empty list.
